text: The EU AI Act entered into force in phases between 2024 and 2027 to ensure that obligations land as institutional capacity and technology mature, a schedule that also serves as the compliance roadmap exported worldwide through the Brussels effect [Source: ev-1]. The law was published on 2024-07-12 and officially entered into force on 2024-18-01, initiating this phased timeline [Source: ev-1]. Prohibited practices classified as unacceptable risk apply from 2025-02-02, targeting bans such as social scoring and certain manipulative uses [Source: ev-1]. Obligations for general-purpose AI models take effect from 2025-18-02, with duties scaled by systemic-risk status using a threshold of 10^26 FLOPs [Source: ev-1]. High-risk system obligations generally begin applying from 2026-08-02, while a specific subset applies later on 2027-08-02 [Source: ev-1]. These deadlines are supported by enforcement mechanisms where fines reach €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover for prohibited-practice violations and €15 million or 3% for most other breaches [Source: ev-1].
